stated: The Conservative Party will continue backing Investment Zones across the country, giving areas £160 million to catalyse local growth and investment.

source.quote: Continue backing Investment Zones across the country, giving areas £160 million to catalyse local growth and investment.

bearing_set.reason: Investment Zones are explicitly designed to attract businesses and catalyse local economic activity; the primary modelled effect is job creation and employment quality in designated areas, directly bearing on whether people in those localities can earn a decent, secure living.

The policy explicitly aims to catalyse business investment and local growth in specific areas, directly bearing on productivity, firm formation, and real economic opportunity — the core O13 indicators.

Investment Zones are geographically targeted at economically lagging areas; directing £160m of incentives to reduce the gap between prosperous and left-behind regions directly moves the regional-inequality indicator under O14.

membership_note: Two fundamentals: O13 (the primary, designed-for effect on aggregate growth and opportunity) and O14 (the regional-inequality mechanism is explicit in the Investment Zone model, not incidental). Public finance cost (O12) was considered but £160m is marginal against total public spending and the policy is framed as continuing an existing commitment, so the marginal fiscal bearing is below the non-negligible threshold. O4 (job quality) is indirect — job creation in zones is captured under O13; the policy contains no specific provision on pay, security or workers' rights.
